hyperedges.label: Manifest-driven build pipeline
hyperedges.rationale: The manifest is the contract: CI validates the schema, the build chain inlines it, and dist/app.js ships the inlined copy.

hyperedges.label: Meeting content pipeline
hyperedges.rationale: Meeting READMEs follow a fixed section order; the reader parses them while the dashboard renders their associated assets.

hyperedges.label: Security and styling constraints
hyperedges.rationale: CSP, the FOUC-blocking theme script, and the CSS token system together constrain how HTML/CSS/JS may be sourced and authored.

nodes.label: Produce/Direct/Semantic Bucket Classification
nodes.rationale: The producer agent must not ship a small crop from a full-page mock as `direct`; the role system exists because bitmap chrome (rounded clipping, shadows, card frames) should be created in code, not baked into raster assets.

nodes.label: Adaptation Is Rethinking, Not Scaling
nodes.rationale: Pushing pixels from desktop to mobile produces broken touch interactions; the actual job is reshaping information architecture and interaction patterns for the new context.

nodes.label: Brand vs Product Motion Register
nodes.rationale: Brand surfaces can afford orchestrated page-load sequences; product surfaces are in-task and cannot make users wait for entrance choreography.

nodes.label: AI Slop Tells Detection
nodes.rationale: AI-generated 'bold' designs converge on the same tells (cyan/purple gradients, glassmorphism, hero metrics, card grids); the audit exists to catch that monoculture before launch.

nodes.label: Anti-AI-Slop Bold Direction
nodes.rationale: Bolder does not mean adding more effects; AI default to cyan/purple gradients, glassmorphism, and neon accents is the opposite of distinctive.

nodes.label: Color Strategies (Restrained/Committed/Full/Drenched)
nodes.rationale: Brand surfaces have permission to exceed the 10% accent rule when the strategy is Committed/Full/Drenched; a beige-and-muted-slate landing page ignores the register.

nodes.label: Reflex-Reject Aesthetic Lanes
nodes.rationale: Aesthetic monoculture (Klim-influenced editorial-typographic) is the second-order training reflex; reject it the same way the font ban list rejects monoculture fonts.

nodes.label: Codex Visual Direction Flow (Steps A-F)
nodes.rationale: Four mandatory user gates exist between shape confirmation and code; compressing them is the dominant failure mode of the craft flow.

nodes.label: Generate Palette Before Mocks
nodes.rationale: Mocks generated against a vague color sense produce noise that drowns out the structural decisions; the confirmed palette is the contract for everything downstream.

nodes.label: OKLCH Perceptually-Uniform Color Space
nodes.rationale: HSL is not perceptually uniform: 50% lightness in yellow looks bright while 50% in blue looks dark, producing visually uneven palette scales.

nodes.label: Dark Mode Surface Scale (lightness not shadow)
nodes.norm_label: dark mode surface scale (lightness not shadow)

nodes.label: Gate Compression Failure Mode
nodes.rationale: Shape confirmation is not a green light to code when the harness has native image generation; it is the green light to begin codex.md Step A.

nodes.label: Critique Orchestration Process
nodes.rationale: The full critique flow: resolve target, compute slug, run two isolated assessments, synthesize report, persist, then ask the user questions. The pairing of human LLM review with deterministic detection is what produces an honest combined score.

nodes.label: Two Isolated Assessments
nodes.rationale: Neither assessment may see the other's output. Running both in one head silently anchors them to each other; do not shortcut for cost, speed, or context-size reasons. This isolation is what makes the combined score honest.

nodes.label: Delight Principles
nodes.rationale: Delight must enhance usability, never obscure it. If users notice the delight more than accomplishing their goal, the delight has gone too far. The principles (amplify never blocks, surprise and discovery, appropriate to context, compound over time) describe a budget, not a license to scatter personality everywhere.

nodes.label: Engaging Loading States
nodes.rationale: Cliched AI loading messages (Herding pixels, Teaching robots to dance, Consulting the magic 8-ball, Counting backwards from infinity) are AI-slop copy. The delight reference explicitly bans them and tells authors to write messages specific to what their product does.

nodes.label: Distill/Simplification Process
nodes.rationale: Perfection is achieved not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away (Saint-Exupery). Simplicity is not about removing features; it is about removing obstacles between users and their goals.

nodes.label: Stitch DESIGN.md Format
nodes.rationale: The frontmatter is the machine-readable layer (what Stitch's linter validates and what the live panel renders tiles from). The prose contextualizes tokens. Tokens are normative; prose provides context for how to apply them.

nodes.label: YAML Frontmatter Schema
nodes.rationale: Stitch validates colors as hex sRGB only; OKLCH/HSL/P3 trigger a linter warning, not a hard error. The choice between hex-in-frontmatter vs OKLCH-in-frontmatter must be a single source of truth; do not split without explicit reason.

nodes.label: Six Section Markdown Body
nodes.rationale: Section headers must match the spec character-for-character so the file stays parseable by other DESIGN.md-aware tools (Stitch, awesome-design-md, skill-rest). Do NOT add extra top-level sections like Layout Principles or Motion.

nodes.label: design.json Sidecar (Extensions Only)
nodes.rationale: The sidecar carries what Stitch's schema can't hold: tonal ramps, shadow/motion/breakpoint tokens, full component HTML/CSS snippets, narrative. It extends the frontmatter, it does not duplicate it.

nodes.label: Component HTML/CSS Translation Rules
nodes.rationale: The panel applies HTML and CSS directly; no post-processing, no framework runtime. Each component must be a self-contained, drop-in snippet (Tailwind utilities expanded to literal CSS, no class references, scoped ds- prefix to avoid collisions).

nodes.label: Pattern Extraction Process
nodes.rationale: Only extract things used 3+ times with the same intent. Premature abstraction is worse than duplication. Design systems grow incrementally; extract what is clearly reusable now, not everything that might someday be reusable.

nodes.label: Hardening Process
nodes.rationale: Designs that only work with perfect data are not production-ready. Harden against the inputs, errors, languages, and network conditions that real users will throw at it.

nodes.label: Issue Severity (P0-P3)
nodes.rationale: If you are unsure between two priority levels, ask: would a user contact support about this? If yes, it is at least P1. This is the calibration test that ties abstract severity bands to real-world cost.

nodes.label: Eight Interactive States
nodes.rationale: Designing hover without focus, or vice versa, is the common miss. They are different. Keyboard users never see hover states, so a focus ring designed for them must be a separate, visible treatment.

nodes.label: Focus Ring Design
nodes.rationale: Never outline:none without replacement. It is an accessibility violation. Use :focus-visible to show focus only for keyboard users; this is the modern, non-performative way to keep the focus ring for the users who need it.

nodes.label: CSS Anchor Positioning
nodes.rationale: The single most common dropdown bug in generated code is position:absolute inside an overflow:hidden container - the dropdown gets clipped. Anchor positioning (Chrome 125+) or position:fixed portals fix this by escaping the stacking context.

nodes.label: Undo Over Confirm for Destructive Actions
nodes.rationale: Users click through confirmations mindlessly. Remove from UI immediately, show an undo toast, then actually delete after the toast expires. Confirmation is reserved for truly irreversible actions (account deletion) and high-cost/batch operations.
nodes.norm_label: undo over confirm for destructive actions

nodes.label: Three Distinct Variant Directions
nodes.rationale: The wrong frame for live mode is show three different design directions. Live runs on an existing surface; the brand has already been chosen. The job is variation within identity, not selection between identities. Default mode is the right mode for ~90% of live sessions.

nodes.label: Identity Lock (Phase A)
nodes.rationale: Write down what you see in one sentence. The sentence describes the surface that is actually on screen; it is not aspirational, not opinionated, not edited toward what the brand should be. Capture, not describe. Be specific - modern is not a color, elegant is not a type pairing.

nodes.label: Departure Mode (Identity Rejected)
nodes.rationale: Departure mode is triggered only by PRODUCT.md anti-references that point at this specific surface or by an explicit user prompt. The cost of being wrong about default is three on-brand variants with similar feel: recoverable. The cost of being wrong about departure is three off-brand variants: unrecoverable.

nodes.label: Carbonize Post-Accept Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Carbonize stitches the accepted variant into source with helper markers and inline CSS so the browser can render with no visual gap. That stitch is temporary; the agent must rewrite into permanent form before doing anything else. Skipping this leaves dead @scope rules and accumulates noise across sessions.

nodes.label: Annotation Reading (Comments and Strokes)
nodes.rationale: Comment position carries meaning. Its {x,y} is element-local CSS px; find the child under that point and apply the comment text locally to that sub-element. A comment near the title is about the title, not a global description.

nodes.label: Easing Curves (Avoid ease)
nodes.rationale: Real objects do not bounce when they stop; they decelerate smoothly. Overshoot effects draw attention to the animation itself rather than the content. Bounce and elastic curves were trendy in 2015 but now feel tacky and amateurish.

nodes.label: Premium Motion Materials
nodes.rationale: The hard rule is not transform and opacity only. The hard rule is: avoid animating layout-driving properties casually, keep expensive effects bounded, and verify in-browser. If blur/filter makes the interaction feel significantly more premium and remains smooth, use it.

nodes.label: Reduced Motion (prefers-reduced-motion)
nodes.rationale: This is not optional. Vestibular disorders affect ~35% of adults over 40. Functional animations like progress bars and loading spinners should still work, just without spatial movement.

nodes.label: Perceived Performance (80ms Threshold)
nodes.rationale: Our brains buffer sensory input for ~80ms to synchronize perception. Anything under 80ms feels instant and simultaneous; this is the target for micro-interactions. Easing affects perceived duration: ease-in toward a task end compresses perceived time.

nodes.label: Carbonize-Required Completion Protocol
nodes.rationale: Completion contract that demands a carbonize step (downstream cleanup of generated artifacts) before the next agent action can fire. Enforced by live-session-store phases and surfaced by live-poll stderr banner and live-complete.mjs.

nodes.label: Durable JSONL-Journal Pattern
nodes.rationale: Append-only JSONL journal + cached JSON snapshot. Powers crash-recovery across live-resume / live-status / live-session-store. Each session has its own journal; snapshot is rebuilt by walking the journal on cold start.

nodes.label: Live Event-Type Vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Canonical event-type strings (generate, variants_ready, agent_done, prefetch, accept, discard, checkpoint, complete, exit) shared implicitly between live-server.validateEvent, live-session-store.applyEvent, and live-completion.completionTypeForAcceptResult. No shared constants file — vocabulary is encoded by string literals in three places.

nodes.label: Variant Wrapper Scaffold (data-impeccable-variants)
nodes.rationale: `<div data-impeccable-variants="v1,v2,v3">` HTML wrapper inserted by live-wrap.wrapCli. The session and variant ids are coordinated by live-server.VARIANT_ID_REGEX; wrappers missing this attribute are detected by live.scanForDrift.

nodes.label: Long-Poll Lease / Ack Protocol
nodes.rationale: Server holds a pending event on a per-agent lease. Agent polls /poll (live-poll) with a lease token. Server replies with accept/discard/timeout. Agent must ack via /reply (live-complete) within PER_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS (270_000). The protocol is the gating mechanism for carbonize_completion_protocol.

nodes.label: Server Auth-Token Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: On start, live-server.findOpenPort binds a port and writes a random UUID token + port to .impeccable/live/server-info. live-poll and live-status read this file via impeccable-paths.readLiveServerInfo and present the token on every request. No JWT, no encryption — entropy is the security floor.

nodes.label: CSP Meta-Tag Patch Protocol
nodes.rationale: Rather than editing the user's CSP policy directly, live-inject stores the original content-security-policy string on a synthetic data-impeccable-csp-original attribute, then injects a relaxed inline meta-tag. patchCspMeta / revertCspMeta are reversible. live.mjs's drift-heal relies on this attribute being present to know whether revert is needed.

nodes.label: globToRegex Duplication Across live-inject / live.mjs
nodes.rationale: Both live-inject.mjs (resolveFiles path) and live.mjs (scanForDrift path) define their own globToRegex helper. The two implementations are functionally identical by design (intentional fallback), but any change to glob semantics must be mirrored in both. There is no shared util — this is acknowledged technical debt.

nodes.label: Pass-Through Proliferation (audit dim 1)
nodes.rationale: All methods either do real work or are trivial module-boundary accessors. No A->B->C delegation chains. Scored 4/4 in every audit.

nodes.label: Information Duplication (audit dim 2)
nodes.rationale: Knowledge items should live in one place; the codebase has multiple instances where the same value (storage key, status string, external host, rel attribute) is hardcoded in 2+ modules. Weakest dimension across audit history, scored 2-3/4.

nodes.label: Interface Documentation (audit dim 3)
nodes.rationale: Coverage 91-100% of public methods across audits. Recurring gaps: setAssetCopyRegistry() and callOnce().

nodes.label: Naming Quality (audit dim 4)
nodes.rationale: Recurring offenders: _processManifestData, generic 'data' in setAssetCopyRegistry, and the catch-all module name utils.js.

nodes.label: Exception Discipline (audit dim 5)
nodes.rationale: Codebase uses built-in Error only; catch blocks mask to safe defaults or warn via ErrorHandler. No rethrow chains. Consistent 4/4.

nodes.label: Tactical Tornado Risk
nodes.rationale: Two-persona assessment (Tactical Tornado + Strategic Thinker) converged on most findings. Risk was MEDIUM in early May, dropped to Low by 2026-05-28 as the video-player listener leak and dead renderHorizonCards calls were addressed.

nodes.label: Event Listener Leak in Video Player (P1)
nodes.rationale: Attaching click listeners to static DOM buttons (resumeBtn, startBtn) inside _setupResumeBar without freeing them when the player is closed or cancelled leads to handler accumulation. When subsequent videos are opened, clicks on these buttons execute all accumulated click handlers in parallel, setting conflicting times and firing multiple overlapping play commands.
nodes.norm_label: event listener leak in video player (p1)

nodes.label: Global Namespace Pollution in Manifests (P2)
nodes.rationale: MANIFEST_DATA and _processManifestData are declared globally outside of IIFEs in manifest.js and _manifest.js, breaking structural consistency with the rest of the codebase where all globals bind explicitly to window.

nodes.label: Storage Keys & Prefix Information Leakage (P2)
nodes.rationale: Namespace prefix 'apbc:' and storage keys (theme, onboarding_dismissed) are hardcoded across multiple files, coupling these modules directly to browser storage interfaces.

nodes.label: Horizon/Drafts Naming Inconsistency (P2)
nodes.rationale: The user interface has transitioned away from the 'Horizon' metaphor to 'Coming Up' and 'Drafts', yet the code retains a dead 'horizon' status in data-meeting.js and horizon-suffixed DOM selectors, creating a mismatch with the actual draft-rendering pipeline.

nodes.label: Dead renderHorizonCards() Call (P0)
nodes.rationale: dashboard.js:121 calls renderHorizonCards() which was removed when the 'horizon' status was deleted from data-meeting.js. When manifest load fails and user clicks retry, this throws ReferenceError. The error-recovery itself is broken.

nodes.label: Three Empty Stub Files in Build (P1)
nodes.rationale: reader-hooks.js, reader-tree.js, reader-toc.js (4 lines each) contain only a comment saying 'Merged into reader-loader.js'. They survive in the source tree and concatenation pipeline, adding download weight and misleading developers about where functionality lives.
nodes.norm_label: three empty stub files in build (p1)

nodes.label: Storage Module Mixes Three Concerns (P1)
nodes.rationale: storage.js:38-118 bundles video resume (sessionStorage), theme persistence (localStorage), and onboarding dismissal (localStorage). Three data domains, two storage mechanisms, different consumers - all in one module. Changing how video resume works risks affecting theme/onboarding code.

nodes.label: Stale JSDoc Lists Removed 'horizon' Status (P1)
nodes.rationale: data-repository.js:59 documents status param as 'One of done, upcoming, horizon, draft' but data-meeting.js:17 only accepts ['done', 'upcoming', 'draft']. 'horizon' was removed from validation but the JSDoc survived.

nodes.label: Internal Constants Exposed as Globals (P2)
nodes.rationale: storage.js:129-130 exports RESUME_MIN_SECONDS (5) and PROGRESS_SAVE_MS (3000) to window. These are tuning constants used only within storage.js:13-14. Exposing them creates an implicit public API contract around private implementation details.

nodes.label: Vestigial __STORAGE_PREFIX Configuration (P2)
nodes.rationale: storage.js:12 and theme-init.js:8 reference window.__STORAGE_PREFIX || 'apbc:'. But __STORAGE_PREFIX is never defined anywhere - the inline script in index.html:20 is blocked by CSP (script-src 'self'). The fallback always wins.

nodes.label: setup.js Dumps 13 DOM Refs to Global (P3)
nodes.rationale: setup.js:25-36 assigns 13 DOM elements to window.*. Every module can couple to any DOM node by name. No encapsulation - renaming an element ID requires auditing every module that reads window[dashboard|reader|etc].
nodes.norm_label: setup.js dumps 13 dom refs to global (p3)

nodes.label: Nested IIFE in toast.js (P3)
nodes.rationale: toast.js:41-56 declares ErrorHandler inside a second IIFE nested inside the main module IIFE. This unique pattern is used nowhere else in the codebase.

nodes.label: Shallow Repository Query Methods (P1)
nodes.rationale: getAll body = return [...this.meetings]; getMeetingById = this.meetings.find(...); getByStatus = this.meetings.filter(...). Repository getters add no abstraction over array methods. The deeper find(criteria) was later introduced to replace them.

nodes.label: Global Export Overexposure (P1)
nodes.rationale: All internal functions exported via window.*. No way to distinguish public API from internal helpers without reading every caller. Changing STORAGE_KEY_PREFIX in storage.js silently breaks every consumer.

nodes.label: Over-Splitting / Classitis (P2)
nodes.rationale: 26 files for 1925 lines (avg 74/file). theme-init.js (28 lines) vs theme.js (69 lines) could merge. asset-copy.js (78 lines) could merge into assets.js (195 lines).

nodes.label: Mixed HTML Construction Strategies (P2)
nodes.rationale: String concatenation in assets.js and dashboard.js vs DOM API in reader-loader.js. Structural DOM errors produce silent rendering failures with no error thrown.

nodes.label: Collapsed Abstraction Layers in reader-loader.js (P1)
nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md describes 4 separate files (hooks, tree, toc, loader) but all are merged into reader-loader.js:1-230 - 230 lines, 11 private functions, 6+ concerns. Each concern changes for different reasons.

nodes.label: Systemic Information Hiding Violation - Flat Window Globals (P1)
nodes.rationale: All 26 files export every function to window.*. Internal functions like loadAssetCopyRegistry and buildStorageKey are globally accessible. When onboarding.js:7 calls buildStorageKey('onboarding_dismissed'), changing STORAGE_KEY_PREFIX in storage.js silently breaks every consumer. Recommended fix: window.APBC = { ... } namespace.
nodes.norm_label: systemic information hiding violation - flat window globals (p1)

nodes.label: Non-Local Cleanup Lifecycle in video-player.js (P2)
nodes.rationale: _wireVideoEvents at video-player.js:86-126 sets up 6+ event listeners and builds a cleanup callback stored in module-level _videoPlayerCleanup. Lifecycle spans 4 functions and a module-level let variable. Forgetting one removeEventListener creates a silent memory leak. Fix: AbortController + AbortSignal.

nodes.label: REL_EXTERNAL 'noopener noreferrer' Duplication (P1)
nodes.rationale: 'noopener noreferrer' rel value duplicated across 3 files (5 locations): viewer.js:62,66, assets.js:76,134, reader-loader.js:30. No single source of truth for external link security policy.

nodes.label: view.officeapps.live.com URL Duplication (P1)
nodes.rationale: view.officeapps.live.com URL duplicated across 3 locations: viewer.js:38, reader-loader.js:15 (allowlist regex), index.html (CSP frame-src). Adding a new viewer origin requires changes in 3 places; CSP and code can drift.

nodes.label: Theme Storage Key Duplication (P2)
nodes.rationale: Theme storage key 'apbc:theme' hardcoded in theme-init.js:17 but composed via STORAGE_KEY_PREFIX + buildStorageKey('theme') in storage.js:14. Changing STORAGE_KEY_PREFIX silently breaks theme persistence.

nodes.label: Meeting Status Strings Duplication (P3)
nodes.rationale: Valid status values 'done', 'upcoming', 'draft' defined in data-meeting.js:17 validStatuses array and re-typed as query strings in dashboard.js:16,88,137. Adding a new status requires changes in 2 modules.

nodes.label: Vague Manifest Loader Naming (P3)
nodes.rationale: _processManifestData (manifest.js:19-24) and generic 'data' (asset-copy.js:17-19) are vague identifiers - readers have to infer whether the code parses, validates, stores, or transforms manifest data.

nodes.label: utils.js Vague Catch-all Name (P3)
nodes.rationale: src/utils.js is a catch-all name (LRU fetch cache + callOnce guard). Invites future accretion of unrelated functions into the same module, reducing cohesion. Recommended rename: markdown-cache.js.

nodes.label: callOnce() Lacks JSDoc (P2)
nodes.rationale: utils.js:46 callOnce() has no JSDoc. Callers must read the implementation to understand the one-shot guard behavior (WeakMap keyed by reference identity).

nodes.label: setAssetCopyRegistry() Lacks JSDoc (P3)
nodes.rationale: asset-copy.js:18 setAssetCopyRegistry() has no JSDoc. Callers can guess it's a setter, but type contract is unclear.

nodes.label: test-hooks.js No-op Window Assignments
nodes.rationale: test-hooks.js:11-17 contains 7 no-op assignments (window.Meeting = window.Meeting) that execute but do nothing - dead code that looks intentional.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages URL Lock-in via Regex
nodes.rationale: reader-loader.js:15 _ALLOWED_EXTERNAL_HOSTS regex bakes GitHub Pages URLs into the rendering pipeline, creating a portability trap for future self-hosters.
nodes.norm_label: github pages url lock-in via regex

nodes.label: IIFE Module Pattern
nodes.rationale: All JS modules are 100% self-contained inside IIFE closures (except manifest.js and _manifest.js). Global state pollution is successfully avoided. This is the foundational encapsulation strategy for the no-framework SPA.

nodes.label: ErrorHandler.warn() Pattern
nodes.rationale: 12 call sites across 7 files use window.ErrorHandler?.warn(...) for operational warnings, making failure paths observable at a single point. Defined in toast.js:41-56 inside a nested IIFE.

nodes.label: AbortController + Generation Counter
nodes.rationale: reader-loader.js:191-225 AbortController + generation counter pattern cancels stale requests, ignores out-of-order responses, enforces 15s timeout. Clean pattern used well. Recommended for video-player.js cleanup lifecycle too.

nodes.label: Deep Caching Abstraction (fetchMarkdown)
nodes.rationale: fetchMarkdown in utils.js caches promises rather than raw string values, which prevents simultaneous redundant network fetches for identical files. LRU eviction with auto-cleanup on reject.

nodes.label: Rigid Security Barrier (isSafePath)
nodes.rationale: path.js:24-43 isSafePath with two DOMAIN enums validates protocol, traversal, absolute paths, control chars, extensions, and roots. Used throughout the app - single source of truth for path safety.

nodes.label: window.APBC Namespace (Proposed)
nodes.rationale: Recommended fix for flat window globals: consolidate into a single namespace object (window.APBC = { storage: { ... }, path: { ... }, ... }). Internal functions stay in IIFE scope, only 15-20 true public API functions on the namespace.

nodes.label: Design Health Score Trend
nodes.rationale: Score trend: 18/20 (2026-05-23) -> 18/20 (2026-05-28 #1) -> 17/20 (2026-05-28 #2) -> 19/20 (2026-05-28 #3). The 5-dimension audits show steady improvement as findings are addressed.

nodes.label: CI Job: validate
nodes.rationale: 15-minute timeout. Runs manifest schema validation, manifest drift check, image size gate (512KB), shellcheck, .nojekyll verify, vendor file verify, hash-route link check, npm ci, npm audit, build:js, build:css, Playwright install + test, link check.

nodes.label: CI Job: deploy (GitHub Pages)

nodes.source_location: Check for unregistered meeting directories step

nodes.label: CI Check: Image Size Gate (512KB)

nodes.label: CI Check: Hash-Route Links Resolve to Files

nodes.label: CI Check: Vendor Files Present

nodes.label: Ghostscript (gs)
nodes.description: External CLI used to rewrite PDFs with /ebook settings (150 dpi, compatibility 1.4).

nodes.label: FFmpeg
nodes.description: External CLI used to transcode video (libx264) and remux audio (AAC).
nodes.rationale: Primary media transcoding engine.

nodes.label: ffprobe
nodes.description: FFmpeg companion used to extract exact duration and file size metadata for the manifest.
nodes.rationale: Metadata source for meeting assets.

nodes.label: Python zipfile module
nodes.description: Standard library used to repackage OOXML at ZIP_DEFLATED compresslevel 9.
nodes.rationale: Dependency-less PPTX compression.

nodes.label: libx264
nodes.description: H.264 video encoder used with CRF 28, preset medium, and a 720p cap.
nodes.rationale: Quality/size sweet spot for meeting recordings.

nodes.label: AAC audio codec
nodes.description: Audio codec used at 128 kbps for both MP4 muxing and M4A remux.
nodes.rationale: Universal compatibility at modest bitrate.

nodes.label: Ghostscript /ebook preset
nodes.description: Picks 150 dpi output and PDF 1.4 compatibility for a strong size/quality balance on slides.

nodes.label: 720p scaling cap
nodes.description: scale='min(1280,iw)':-2 keeps height ≤ 720 while preserving aspect ratio.
nodes.rationale: Bounds bitrate for small repo-friendly video.

nodes.label: CRF 28 quality target
nodes.description: Constant Rate Factor 28 with preset medium prioritises compression over perceptual fidelity.

nodes.label: +faststart moov flag
nodes.description: Relocates the moov atom so MP4s can start streaming before the file is fully downloaded.

nodes.label: ZIP compresslevel 9
nodes.description: Maximum deflate level chosen to squeeze every byte from the OOXML container.
nodes.rationale: Lossless repackaging with no quality trade-off.

nodes.label: NN-Slug naming convention
nodes.description: Two-digit zero-padded meeting number followed by a kebab-case slug, with optional recording-type suffix (deep-dive/critique/debate).

nodes.label: EXTENSION_MAPPING table
nodes.description: Maps mp4/m4a → recordings, pptx/pdf → slides, png/jpg/jpeg/gif/svg/webp → resources, kept in sync with src/01-utils.js.

nodes.label: KNOWN_RECORDING_TYPES
nodes.description: Allowed --type values for podcast recordings: deep-dive, critique, debate.

nodes.label: Alternate asset detection
nodes.description: Regex on -alt/_alt/-alternate/_alternate in the basename adds an -alternate suffix and records provenance in asset-manifest.json.

nodes.label: Dry-run mode
nodes.description: Prints the planned rename, target dir, and manifest update without moving files or modifying state.

nodes.label: Interactive y/N confirmation
nodes.description: Reads confirmation from stdin before performing the move, unless --dry-run is set.

nodes.label: Meeting folder inference
nodes.description: If --meeting is omitted and exactly one meetings/meeting-NN directory exists, infers that meeting number.

nodes.label: set -euo pipefail
nodes.description: All four .sh wrappers enable strict mode so any unhandled failure propagates and undefined variables abort the script.

nodes.label: Bash → Python exec wrapper
nodes.description: Each .sh script is a 1-liner that execs the matching .py with strict mode, giving Claude a uniform shell surface while keeping the logic in Python.

nodes.label: Size-reduction reporting
nodes.description: All three compress scripts compute ((orig-new)/orig)*100 and print original KB / new KB / reduction percentage.

nodes.label: Output file verification
nodes.description: Each compressor asserts the output exists and has non-zero size before declaring success.

nodes.label: FFmpeg format-fallback pass
nodes.description: If the primary video transcode yields no output, retries with an explicit -f <ext> mux option.

nodes.label: Post-compression metadata capture
nodes.description: After compression, ffprobe + stat extract floored duration and KB size, then write to docs/manifest.json (duration in seconds, fileSize in MB).

nodes.label: Unconditional compression policy
nodes.description: Every meeting asset is compressed regardless of original size — no threshold gate, no confirmation dialog.

nodes.label: Floor, never round, durations
nodes.description: int() truncation ensures the manifest never overstates playback time.

nodes.label: Jaccard similarity
nodes.description: Set-theoretic overlap ratio |A∩B|/|A∪B| used to score shared vocabulary between two services.

nodes.label: Explicit coupling verdict
nodes.description: Overlap exists and an import edge is present — coupling is visible and not a CI failure.

nodes.label: No-coupling verdict
nodes.description: Jaccard score below the threshold — services are deemed vocabulary-isolated.

nodes.label: Default Jaccard threshold 0.10
nodes.description: 10% overlap is the default cutoff for flagging hidden coupling; tunable via --threshold.

nodes.label: Tri-state CI exit codes
nodes.description: 0 = clean, 1 = hidden coupling detected (CI fail), 2 = usage error.

nodes.label: JSON report output
nodes.description: --json emits shared_terms_count, jaccard_score, has_import_edge, threshold, coupling_verdict, and the ranked shared_terms list.

nodes.label: Human-readable text report
nodes.description: Default rendering includes service term counts, ranked shared terms, Jaccard %, import edge status, and a verdict banner.

nodes.label: Import edge detection
nodes.description: Regexes import|require(|include|use for the other service's basename to classify coupling as explicit vs hidden.

nodes.label: Identifier splitting strategies
nodes.description: Splits identifiers on _, -, SCREAMING_SNAKE boundaries, and CamelCase humps, then lowercases and filters stop words and tokens < 3 chars.

nodes.label: Stop words filter
nodes.description: Hard-coded set of language keywords and common English words (return, class, def, the, and, of, ...) pruned from tokens.

nodes.label: DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS set
nodes.description: Default scanned extensions covering 18 languages plus .md/.txt: .js .ts .py .go .java .rb .rs .c .h .cpp .cs .php .kt .swift .scala .jsx .tsx .md .txt.

nodes.label: String literal stripping
nodes.description: Replaces single/double/backtick strings and triple-quoted blocks with whitespace so the token regex doesn't pick up prose.

nodes.label: Block comment stripping
nodes.description: Strips /* */ and <!-- --> comments; deliberately keeps // line comments because they often encode domain terms.

nodes.label: Shared term ranking
nodes.description: Sorts shared terms by descending combined frequency (freq_a + freq_b), supports --min-freq and --top slicing.

nodes.label: Directory walk filtering
nodes.description: should_skip prunes node_modules, vendor, .git, dist, build, target, .next, etc. during os.walk to keep noise out of the audit.

nodes.label: Bavota coupling research
nodes.description: Underlying research the skill is based on — vocabulary overlap as a proxy for hidden coupling even when no import edge exists.

nodes.label: Remediation via versioned schemas
nodes.description: When hidden coupling surfaces, formalize the shared vocabulary with a protobuf, JSON Schema, or published type package.

nodes.label: TestTokenization
nodes.description: unittest.TestCase covering camel/snake/kebab/screaming case splits, stop-word stripping, short-token filter, string-literal skipping, and a mixed-case fixture file.

nodes.label: TestExtractNouns
nodes.description: Verifies extract_nouns pulls the expected nouns (order, state, payment, fulfillment, status) from a hidden-coupling fixture.

nodes.label: TestJaccardOverlap
nodes.description: Covers identical sets (1.0), disjoint sets (0.0), partial overlap (0.5), and empty union (0.0).

nodes.label: TestDetectImportEdges
nodes.description: Asserts that the hidden-coupling fixtures have no cross-import and the explicit-coupling fixtures do.

nodes.label: TestHiddenCouplingDetection
nodes.description: Asserts exit code 1 for hidden coupling, exit code 0 for explicit coupling (visible import), and exit code 0 for the no-overlap fixture.

nodes.label: TestUsageErrors
nodes.description: Verifies exit code 2 for missing directories, out-of-range thresholds, and that --json output is valid JSON.

nodes.label: TestReportOutput
nodes.description: Smoke-tests --json rendering against the hidden-coupling fixture.

nodes.label: hidden-coupling fixture tree
nodes.description: Two service trees (A and B) sharing domain nouns (order, payment, fulfillment) with no import edge — drives the 'hidden' verdict.

nodes.label: explicit-coupling fixture tree
nodes.description: Two service trees with overlapping vocabulary AND a real import edge — should produce the 'explicit' verdict (exit 0).

nodes.label: no-overlap fixture tree
nodes.description: Disjoint vocabularies — used to confirm a clean exit 0.

nodes.label: tokenization/mixed_case.py fixture
nodes.description: Python file combining OrderState, RetryCount, PaymentIntent, and CalculateAmount — exercises all identifier-splitting paths.

nodes.label: Explicit Coupling Order Service
nodes.description: Python fixture for service A in the explicit-coupling scenario. Imports service_b.invoice and shares domain vocabulary.
nodes.rationale: Test fixture used to verify vocabulary-audit detects coupling when both an import and shared vocabulary are present.

nodes.label: Explicit Coupling Invoice Service
nodes.description: JavaScript fixture for service B in the explicit-coupling scenario. Exports generateInvoice and notifyFulfillment for service A.
nodes.rationale: Paired fixture with order.py; provides the imports and shared symbols that produce the explicit coupling signal.

nodes.label: Hidden Coupling Order Service
nodes.description: Python fixture for the hidden-coupling scenario. Contains the same shared vocabulary as invoice.js but no import statement.
nodes.rationale: Used to verify vocabulary-audit catches semantic coupling even when there is no syntactic dependency.

nodes.label: Hidden Coupling Invoice Service
nodes.description: JavaScript fixture for the hidden-coupling scenario. Mirrors order.py vocabulary without imports.
nodes.rationale: Sister fixture exercising the audit's semantic-only detection path.

nodes.label: No-Overlap Weather Service
nodes.description: Go fixture exposing Temperature, Forecast, and ConvertWindSpeed. Contains zero shared vocabulary with calendar.js.
nodes.rationale: Negative control that ensures the audit does not flag coincidental identifier overlap.

nodes.label: No-Overlap Calendar Service
nodes.description: JavaScript fixture exposing CalendarEvent and scheduleReminder. Domain is events, not weather.
nodes.rationale: Negative control; verifies audit specificity against true negatives.

nodes.label: Mixed-Case Tokenization Test
nodes.description: Python fixture exercising identifier tokenization across snake_case, kebab-case, camelCase, and PascalCase within a single class.
nodes.rationale: Validates that the audit's tokenizer handles all common identifier styles uniformly.

nodes.label: OrderState (Shared Vocabulary)
nodes.description: Enum-like value used by both order.py and invoice.js to model the lifecycle of an order.
nodes.rationale: The clearest shared semantic signal that the audit is designed to detect.

nodes.label: PaymentIntent (Shared Vocabulary)
nodes.description: Identifier appearing in both service A (process_payment) and service B (generateInvoice, PaymentIntent.findById).
nodes.rationale: Domain term shared across services, indicating semantic coupling around the payment flow.

nodes.label: FulfillmentStatus (Shared Vocabulary)
nodes.description: Enum-like return value used by OrderService.fulfill_order and propagated through notifyFulfillment.
nodes.rationale: Couples the order and invoice services around shipment outcomes.

nodes.label: OrderService Class
nodes.description: Service A's order management class with create_order, process_payment, and fulfill_order methods.
nodes.rationale: Public surface of the order domain whose vocabulary leaks into service B.

nodes.label: Temperature Struct
nodes.description: Go struct with Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Humidity fields. Used by Forecast.
nodes.rationale: Pure weather-domain construct, no overlap with calendar vocabulary.

nodes.label: CalendarEvent Class
nodes.description: ES6 class modeling calendar entries with title, startDate, endDate, and location.
nodes.rationale: Domain construct in the no-overlap baseline; should not be flagged by the audit.

nodes.label: OrderStateManager Class
nodes.description: Mixed-case class combining MAX_RETRY_COUNT, payment_intent_id, and a kebab-case identifier in one body.
nodes.rationale: Designed to stress the tokenization pipeline with multiple naming conventions at once.

nodes.label: generateInvoice Function
nodes.description: Builds an invoice payload from a PaymentIntent. Returns an object with orderState and fulfillmentStatus.
nodes.rationale: Concrete site where shared vocabulary (orderState, fulfillmentStatus) materializes in service B.

nodes.label: notifyFulfillment Function
nodes.description: Async function that calls NotificationService.send with orderId and fulfillmentStatus.
nodes.rationale: Another vector for shared vocabulary propagation between services.

nodes.label: Forecast Function
nodes.description: Returns a hard-coded Temperature struct; pure weather domain.
nodes.rationale: Used in the no-overlap baseline to keep service A self-contained.

nodes.label: scheduleReminder Function
nodes.description: Schedules a reminder for an eventId at a future timestamp.
nodes.rationale: Domain function in service B; completes the no-overlap pair.

nodes.label: Explicit Coupling Pattern
nodes.description: Coupling detectable by both syntactic imports and shared vocabulary. order.py imports service_b.invoice and reuses OrderState/PaymentIntent/FulfillmentStatus.
nodes.rationale: Defines the positive case the audit must always report.

nodes.label: Hidden Coupling Pattern
nodes.description: Coupling where services share vocabulary but have no import edge. The audit must still surface this risk.
nodes.rationale: Defines the semantic-only detection path that distinguishes the audit from a plain import linter.

nodes.label: Vocabulary Audit Concept
nodes.description: Static analysis technique that surfaces hidden semantic coupling between services by comparing tokenized identifiers across module boundaries.
nodes.rationale: Skill-level concept that unifies the fixture scenarios under one detection philosophy.

nodes.label: Identifier Tokenization
nodes.description: Process of splitting identifiers (snake_case, kebab-case, camelCase, PascalCase, SCREAMING_SNAKE) into comparable tokens.
nodes.rationale: First stage of the audit pipeline; its correctness determines detection accuracy.

nodes.label: Inlined Manifest Module
nodes.description: Generated module that exposes window.MANIFEST_DATA containing meetings, assetCopy, and additional meeting fields like video, slides, and additional_material.
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for the runtime; rebuilt from docs/manifest.json by inline-manifest.cjs.

nodes.label: App Entry Module
nodes.description: IIFE that wires initTheme, initRouting, asset click delegation, manifest loading, and dashboard rendering at startup.
nodes.rationale: Application entry point; orchestrates all subsystems.

nodes.label: Asset Copy Registry
nodes.description: Registry mapping asset copy types (alternate, deep-dive, critique, debate) to label/title/icon/color. Validates manifest entries and exposes loadAssetCopyRegistry and getAssetCopy.
nodes.rationale: Centralizes asset copy presentation so changes only happen in one place.

nodes.label: Asset Click Delegation
nodes.description: Sets up delegated click handlers on [data-asset-container] elements; routes .mp4 links to openVideoPlayer and other links to navigation.
nodes.rationale: Single handler pattern that avoids per-row listener attachment.

nodes.label: Asset Builder Module
nodes.description: Defines buildAssetRows plus its primary-row, additional-row, resource-strip, and podcast-disclosure helpers. Exposes buildAssetRows, buildPodcastDisclosure, buildAdditionalRow, buildAdditionalSummary on window.
nodes.rationale: Encapsulates HTML generation for all asset surfaces; viewer URL resolution is delegated to viewer.js.

nodes.label: showDashboardRenderError
nodes.description: Renders a dashboard render error in the upcoming card header and triggers a toast.
nodes.rationale: Failure-path user feedback for dashboard render errors.

nodes.label: loadAssetCopyRegistry
nodes.description: Validates and installs the asset copy registry from manifest, warning on missing/extra keys and falling back to defaults.
nodes.rationale: Manifest integration boundary; sanitizes inputs before they reach renderers.

nodes.label: getAssetCopy
nodes.description: Returns the merged entry for a copy type, with manifest overrides layered on top of DEFAULT_ASSET_COPY.
nodes.rationale: Read accessor for asset copy used by buildAdditionalRow and friends.

nodes.label: buildAdditionalRow
nodes.description: Builds a row for one additional material item, choosing icon/color from getAssetCopy(category) and an audio fallback for m4a/mp3/wav/ogg.
nodes.rationale: Ties asset-copy registry to row rendering; integration with tokenization of category labels.

nodes.label: buildResourceStrip
nodes.description: Renders a horizontal strip of image thumbnails (with webp sources) for image-type additional_material items.
nodes.rationale: Compact visual presentation of resource images.

nodes.label: buildPodcastDisclosure
nodes.description: Wraps podcast rows in a <details> element with a chevron and a summary label.
nodes.rationale: Disclosure pattern keeps the dashboard card compact while allowing expansion.

nodes.label: buildAdditionalSummary
nodes.description: Builds a summary string like 'Additional Resources: 1 Video · 3 Podcasts' from additional_material.
nodes.rationale: Used as the disclosure summary label in buildPodcastDisclosure.

nodes.label: _toAssetSlug
nodes.description: Extracts a URL-safe slug from a file path; lowercased, extension stripped, non-alphanumerics replaced with dashes.
nodes.rationale: Drives deterministic DOM ids for asset rows so tests can target them.

nodes.label: ASSET_COPY Registry (Module State)
nodes.description: Module-private state holding the validated asset copy registry, populated by loadAssetCopyRegistry and read by getAssetCopy.
nodes.rationale: Encapsulates asset copy state inside the IIFE, exposing a narrow public API on window.

nodes.label: Manifest-Driven UI
nodes.description: Architecture where docs/manifest.json is the canonical schedule and the runtime renders meetings, videos, slides, and additional material from that single source.
nodes.rationale: Avoids per-meeting code paths and keeps the deployment artifact small.

nodes.label: Asset Copy Registry Pattern
nodes.description: Validates and centralizes label/title/icon/color for asset copy types with defaults and overrides.
nodes.rationale: Lets the manifest evolve presentation without touching renderers.

nodes.label: Click Delegation on Data-Asset-Container
nodes.description: Pattern of attaching a single click listener per [data-asset-container] rather than per asset row, routing to either the video player or navigation based on path classification.
nodes.rationale: Reduces listener count and keeps behavior consistent for dynamically rendered rows.

nodes.label: APOSD Viewer URL Delegation
nodes.description: assets.js delegates PPTX viewer URL construction to viewer.js (APOSD Principle 3) to keep this module focused on row HTML.
nodes.rationale: Pulls a non-trivial decision out of assets.js so it can be tested in isolation.

nodes.label: MANIFEST_DATA Global
nodes.description: Top-level object on window holding the meetings array and assetCopy registry, generated at build time from docs/manifest.json.
nodes.rationale: Global handoff between build artifacts and runtime modules.

nodes.label: Meeting Schema (manifest)
nodes.description: Shape of a meeting entry: id, session, date, title, status, color, wash, readmeUrl, keyTakeaway, video, slides, additional_material.
nodes.rationale: Contract between the manifest build step and the runtime renderers.

nodes.label: AssetCopy Registry Schema
nodes.description: Object with keys alternate, deep-dive, critique, debate; each entry is {label, title, icon?, color?} validated at load time.
nodes.rationale: Defines the exact shape of MANIFEST_DATA.assetCopy and the validation rules in loadAssetCopyRegistry.

nodes.label: Dashboard Module
nodes.description: Renders the dashboard's three card sections (upcoming, archive, draft) and wires a retry UI when the manifest fails to load.
nodes.rationale: Encapsulates the visual presentation layer for meeting cards on the home page.

nodes.label: Format Utilities
nodes.description: Pure helpers: escapeHTML(), formatDuration(), formatFileSize().
nodes.rationale: Centralizes HTML escaping and human-readable number formatting used across modules.

nodes.label: Manifest Loader
nodes.description: Loads the meeting manifest from inline data or via fetch (8s timeout) and seeds the MeetingRepository.
nodes.rationale: Bridges the build-time manifest and the runtime data layer.

nodes.label: Onboarding Banner
nodes.description: Manages a dismissible first-visit onboarding banner with localStorage persistence and a global restore action.
nodes.rationale: Onboards new readers while letting returning visitors skip the message.

nodes.label: Path Validation
nodes.description: Exports isSafePath() and the DOMAIN enum to block traversal, protocol, and extension abuse in repo and asset paths.
nodes.rationale: Hardens fetch targets to the repo's known roots before any network call.

nodes.label: Content Link Rewriter
nodes.description: Rewrites <a> hrefs in rendered markdown: .md -> '#p=' and asset links -> viewer URLs; disables unsafe targets.
nodes.rationale: Converts raw markdown links into safe hash routes and asset viewers.

nodes.label: Retry UI
nodes.description: bindRetryButton() and showRetryUI() render a centered retry panel with optimistic disabled state.
nodes.rationale: Reusable failure-state UI shared by manifest and reader error paths.

nodes.label: Hash Router
nodes.description: Parses window.location.hash (#p=...) and dispatches to registered handlers; validates paths before dispatch.
nodes.rationale: Decouples URL parsing from view-specific rendering for static-host hash navigation.

nodes.label: renderDraftCards
nodes.description: Renders draft (planned) meetings with placeholder content and 'Planned' badge.
nodes.rationale: Keeps upcoming themes visible even before materials exist.

nodes.label: setupManifestRetryUI
nodes.description: Clears dashboard containers and shows a retry prompt; reloads manifest and re-renders all sections on retry.
nodes.rationale: Defines the failure UX for the dashboard's central data dependency.

nodes.label: _renderCardHeader
nodes.description: Builds the shared card header: session meta line, title, and an optional badge.
nodes.rationale: Eliminates duplication between upcoming, archive, and draft cards.

nodes.label: _renderCardBadge
nodes.description: Renders a small uppercase badge with configurable border and text color.
nodes.rationale: Supports the 'Upcoming', 'Done', and 'Planned' labels.

nodes.label: _renderSessionMeta
nodes.description: Renders the 'Session X • Date' metadata line shared by every card type.
nodes.rationale: Centralizes the eye-catching session header styling.

nodes.label: _renderCardList
nodes.description: Generic card-list renderer that toggles section visibility based on a result count.
nodes.rationale: Avoids 'empty section' UI when no meetings match a status.

nodes.label: Meeting class
nodes.description: Validating constructor that materializes a Meeting from a raw manifest entry; throws on missing id/title/status.
nodes.rationale: Defines errors out of existence: invalid meetings never enter the repository.

nodes.label: Meeting.hasVideo
nodes.description: Returns true only when status is 'done' and a video file is present.
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for the 'should we show a video player?' check.

nodes.label: MeetingRepository.find
nodes.description: Compound query: no args returns all; {id} returns one or null; {status} returns an array.
nodes.rationale: One deep method replaces three thin ones, simplifying callers.

nodes.label: escapeHTML
nodes.description: Replaces &, <, >, ", ' with HTML entities to prevent XSS during string interpolation.
nodes.rationale: The project's only XSS defense in the rendering layer.

nodes.label: formatDuration
nodes.description: Formats seconds as 'Xh Ym' or 'Xm Ys'; returns '' on invalid input.
nodes.rationale: Used in the video/recording row of meeting cards.

nodes.label: formatFileSize
nodes.description: Formats MB into KB (<1), decimal MB (<10), or integer MB; returns '' on invalid input.
nodes.rationale: Renders file sizes on the asset rows of meeting cards.

nodes.label: loadManifest
nodes.description: Resolves inline data (__MANIFEST_DATA) or fetches docs/manifest.json with an 8s AbortController timeout.
nodes.rationale: Reduces first-render latency by preferring build-time inlined data.

nodes.label: findMeetings
nodes.description: Thin facade over MeetingRepository.find; returns [] when the manifest has not yet loaded.
nodes.rationale: Single public query surface for the rest of the app.

nodes.label: _initializeManifestState
nodes.description: Constructs a new MeetingRepository, hydrates it, and loads the asset copy registry.
nodes.rationale: Encapsulates the side-effect-laden transition from raw JSON to typed state.

nodes.label: fetchMarkdown
nodes.description: LRU-cached fetch that returns a Promise; evicts on rejection to avoid caching errors.
nodes.rationale: Caches promise objects so concurrent in-flight requests share a single network call.

nodes.label: callOnce
nodes.description: One-shot guard keyed by reference identity (WeakMap).
nodes.rationale: Prevents duplicate DOM event listener registration across re-renders.

nodes.label: LRU Markdown Cache
nodes.description: 20-entry Map-based LRU keyed by repo path, implemented as delete+set on hit.
nodes.rationale: Tuned for the project's actual catalog size (a dozen meetings).

nodes.label: initOnboardingBanner
nodes.description: Reads dismissed state, mounts the banner, and wires dismiss + restore (callOnce-guarded) handlers.
nodes.rationale: Ensures the dismiss listener is registered only once even if called repeatedly.

nodes.label: getOnboardingDismissed
nodes.description: Reads the localStorage flag; logs and returns false on storage failure.
nodes.rationale: Tolerates Safari private mode and quota errors without breaking the page.

nodes.label: setOnboardingDismissed
nodes.description: Writes or removes the localStorage flag; logs and swallows storage errors.
nodes.rationale: Symmetric counterpart to getOnboardingDismissed.

nodes.label: isSafePath
nodes.description: Rejects protocol URLs, traversal, absolute paths, control chars, and roots outside the allowlist; enforces .md for REPO and a media extension list for ASSET.
nodes.rationale: First line of defense before any network fetch or link rewrite.

nodes.label: DOMAIN enum
nodes.description: Frozen {REPO, ASSET} enum used by isSafePath and link rewriter to switch root and extension rules.
nodes.rationale: Cuts the path-validation surface into two purpose-specific modes.

nodes.label: rewriteContentLinks
nodes.description: Walks every <a> in the container, resolves relative hrefs against docPath, and rewrites them to '#p=...' or to a viewer URL; disables unsafe links.
nodes.rationale: Translates raw markdown links into the app's hash-route + viewer conventions.

nodes.label: _disableLink
nodes.description: Strips href, sets aria-disabled='true' and an optional title on a link element.
nodes.rationale: Communicates 'unavailable' to assistive tech without removing the link from the DOM.

nodes.label: loadPage
nodes.description: Fetches, parses, sanitizes, and renders a markdown document; uses a generation counter and AbortController to cancel stale loads and a 15s timeout.
nodes.rationale: Single entry point for the reader; safe under fast navigation.

nodes.label: buildTableOfContents
nodes.description: Generates a TOC <nav> from the document's h2 elements; returns null if fewer than two sections exist.
nodes.rationale: Improves navigability of long meeting notes without cluttering short ones.

nodes.label: _applyMeetingMaterialsTree
nodes.description: Finds the 'Meeting Materials' h2 and converts its following UL into a tree with ARIA treeitem/group roles.
nodes.rationale: Wires the convention into a navigable, screen-reader-friendly tree.

nodes.label: _scrollToElement
nodes.description: Focuses the target and computes an explicit scroll position that subtracts the sticky header height.
nodes.rationale: Workaround for cross-browser scrollIntoView offset inconsistency.

nodes.label: default-src 'none' Directive

nodes.label: The One Thing Rule
nodes.description: Uncle Bob's principle that functions should do exactly one thing, ideally in 2-4 lines.
nodes.rationale: Core tenet of Clean Code's decomposition philosophy.

nodes.label: Shallow Interfaces
nodes.description: Ousterhout's critique term for functions whose small interface does not justify their existence.
nodes.rationale: Critique of Uncle Bob's tiny-function style.

nodes.label: Entanglement
nodes.description: State of code where scattered microscopic functions share implicit state, forcing the reader to mentally stitch the system back together.
nodes.rationale: A primary critique term used by Ousterhout.

nodes.label: Working Memory Limit (~7 items)
nodes.description: Psychological fact that humans hold only ~7 concepts at once, used to justify both sides' positions.
nodes.rationale: Empirical anchor for the cognitive load discussion.

nodes.label: Method Length Debate
nodes.description: The first battleground: should functions be 2-4 lines (Bob) or as long as needed for depth (John)?
nodes.rationale: First major sub-debate in the transcripts.

nodes.label: Comments Are Always Failures
nodes.description: Uncle Bob's absolute stance that comments represent a failure to express intent in code, prone to rotting and lying.
nodes.rationale: Bob's most absolutist position in the debate.

nodes.label: Mega-syllabic Names
nodes.description: Uncle Bob's alternative to comments: extremely long descriptive names like 'isLeastRelevantMultipleOfLargerPrimeFactor'.
nodes.rationale: Concrete style choice that exemplifies the comments-as-failures position.

nodes.label: Abstraction Leak
nodes.description: When a name-based abstraction fails because underlying behavior contradicts what the name implies.
nodes.rationale: Mechanism by which Ousterhout argues small functions fail.

nodes.label: TDD Red-Green-Refactor Loop
nodes.description: The micro-iteration cycle of writing a failing test, making it pass, then refactoring, championed by Uncle Bob.
nodes.rationale: Core tactical method on Bob's side.

nodes.label: Bundling Approach (Strategic Design)
nodes.description: Ousterhout's method: sketch the full design in pencil, write code to support it, then test the bundle. Think deeply before typing.
nodes.rationale: Counter-position to TDD's micro-iterations.

nodes.label: Tactical Myopia
nodes.description: Ousterhout's term for TDD's near-sightedness, where solving the next micro-test blinds developers to the larger architecture.
nodes.rationale: Core critique of TDD from the strategic-design side.

nodes.label: Psychological Safety of TDD
nodes.description: Uncle Bob's argument that TDD's tight feedback loop enables fearless refactoring and 'trust with your life' test suites.
nodes.rationale: The emotional/practical benefit Bob uses to defend TDD.

nodes.label: Code as Truth
nodes.description: Uncle Bob's epistemological stance: only code is verified by the compiler; comments drift and lie.
nodes.rationale: Underlying philosophy behind the comments-are-failures stance.

nodes.label: Context Switch Heuristic
nodes.description: Proposed metric: count the number of file/method jumps a developer must make in their IDE to trace a single state change.
nodes.rationale: Critique-suggested objective replacement for line-counting.

nodes.label: State Tracking Limit
nodes.description: Proposed heuristic: a method is over-decomposed if a parent must pass the same 3-4 variables through a deep extraction chain.
nodes.rationale: Operationalizes the cognitive load critique.

nodes.label: Dependency Graphs over Line Counts
nodes.description: Proposed alternative: a decomposition is only valid if children can be understood without cross-referencing siblings.
nodes.rationale: Structural metric for evaluating extraction quality.

nodes.label: Executable Specifications
nodes.description: Suggested bridge between English comments and code: type constraints, contracts, and tests that the compiler enforces.
nodes.rationale: Critique's proposed synthesis of the comments-vs-code dichotomy.

nodes.label: Strict Typing and RustDoc

nodes.rationale: Concrete instance of executable specifications.

nodes.label: Benchmark-Linked Comments

nodes.rationale: Specific application of executable-specs to optimization justifications.

Both files open with an identical Register section that frames decisions as brand vs product - same dichotomy, two different surfaces. The brand register favors distributed personality; the product register favors moments only.
Both cover the same kind of non-content moments (loading, empty). Delight leans on personality/playful copy; onboard leans on value proposition and a CTA. Same surface, different authoring intent.

Both files want a satisfying first-time user moment - onboard's aha moment is what celebration moments are designed around. Time to value is the goal; celebration is the surface treatment of achieving it.

Interaction simplification recommends fewer states/options; interaction-design's 8 states argues every state must be designed. Tension, not contradiction - simplify the count of choices users face, but every state of the surviving choices still needs design.
Progressive disclosure (onboard) and interaction simplification (distill) both argue for hiding complexity until needed; they just sequence the reveal differently (over time vs once-and-done).

Layout forbids the hero metric layout (big number, small label, gradient) as a template; distill forbids removing functionality for simplicity. Same structural anti-pattern: a default template that reads as a single answer when the problem needs choice.
Document assumes a design system exists or fabricates one from tokens; extract is the upstream step that discovers and consolidates the tokens/components document will formalize.

Live identity extraction reads DESIGN.md as the authoritative source (step 1) and falls back to CSS/computed styles when absent. The two skills form an identity pipeline: document captures the system, live enforces it during variant generation.
Document's frontmatter is the consumer of extract's output - extract discovers hard-coded values worth promoting to tokens, document writes them into the machine-readable layer.

The pitfalls section is precisely the failure mode of breaking the six-section constraint. Don't add Layout Principles, Motion, or Responsive Behavior; fold into the six spec sections where it belongs.

The Creative North Star (document) and the Identity Lock sentence (live) both anchor what a brand is. North Star is aspirational prose; Identity Lock is observational capture. Same role, different authoring direction.

Both locate and reuse existing code structure rather than rewriting - extract promotes repeated patterns to a system, live-wrap locates the source file for an element before variant generation. Same philosophy, different scale.
Layout's spacing system (clamp tokens, gap, semantic scale) is the same kind of artifact extract promotes to a design token.
Text overflow (long words, wrapping) and i18n text expansion (German ~30% longer) hit the same CSS mechanisms: word-wrap, overflow-wrap, clamp(), and flex/grid min-width: 0.

Onboard treats empty states as an onboarding opportunity; harden treats them as a boundary condition. Same component, different priority - onboard argues for personality and CTAs; harden argues for clear next action and resilience.
Both files warn against premature optimization - harden throttling/debouncing should be deliberate; motion-design warns will-change should only be set when animation is imminent, not preemptively.

The 100/300/500ms rule maps directly to state transitions in interaction-design's 8 states: instant feedback (100-150ms for press/toggle), state changes (200-300ms for menu open), layout changes (300-500ms for modal).
Both use focus-visible / focus management as the mechanism. Modals need focus trapping (inert, dialog); focus rings need :focus-visible - same underlying accessibility primitive.

Both files advocate optimistic UI: motion-design's preemptive start (begin transitions while loading) maps to interaction-design's optimistic updates (show success immediately, rollback on failure). Same psychology, different surfaces.

Undo toast is a lightweight alternative to a confirmation modal - the destructive action argues for skipping modals entirely. Both reach for the same goal (prevent accidental data loss) through opposite means.

Layout defines a semantic z-index scale (dropdown 100, modal-backdrop 300, modal 400, tooltip 600); interaction-design's anchor positioning / top-layer pattern places popovers above the scale, escaping the z-index war entirely.

Both define the same `density` param spec: a range slider (layout: 0.6-1.4, live: 0-1 depending on action) that drives --p-density CSS var used to scale spacing tokens. Layout names it as a MUST for the layout action; live mode uses it as a default composition knob.
Both define a `structure` steps param with stacked/grid/bento options that branches scoped CSS by data-p-structure attribute. Same concept, same spec, different default labels.
